title: They weren’t just baking bread.
paragraphs:
They weren’t just baking bread.
They were breathing in the stench of their own sin.
Because this isn’t just Ezekiel’s story.
God told a prophet to cook food over dung.

What if what you’ve normalized…
Heaven calls defiled?
What if the thing you’ve been hiding, managing, renaming…
“Ah, Lord God! Behold, I have never defiled myself…” (Ezekiel 4:14)
And God’s message hit like thunder—
“My people will eat defiled bread among the nations…” (Ezekiel 4:13)
Some of you aren’t struggling with “big sins.”
You’re just slowly getting used to small compromises.
That lust you scroll through at midnight?
That double life you’ve learned to balance?
You don’t even recognize who you’ve become.
This is the horror of Ezekiel 4.
Because sometimes the most loving thing God can do…
Is show you how far you’ve drifted.
And here’s the emotional trigger you can’t escape:
Not the fake kind people throw around.
The kind you feel when you’re alone.
“This is not who you were made to be.”
Because if all you see is shame…
Ezekiel was told to cook over dung…
But Jesus stepped into a world already covered in it.
He didn’t stand at a distance.
He walked into places religious people avoided.
“God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us…” (2 Corinthians 5:21)
Jesus didn’t just see your sin.
Every moment you chose darkness over light.
“Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow…” (Isaiah 1:18)
But here’s the line most people don’t want to cross:
“I don’t want to live like this anymore.”
Some scholars interpret Ezekiel 4 as symbolic of Israel’s exile and spiritual corruption.
So what are you still holding onto?
What are you still calling “not that bad”?
What are you still hiding behind filters and excuses?
God is not exposing you to shame you.
He is exposing you to save you.
You don’t need to clean yourself first.
Because Jesus doesn’t heal fake people.
Say it in your heart if you mean it:
Not because you read a post.
But because the Spirit is knocking.
It might be the doorway to freedom.
